opportunity.note: Availability, engagement, and compensation are set by the member. They are self-declared preferences, not verified terms.

efficiency.note: Efficiency signals, not a ranking. Producing the same verified result with fewer tokens is better. Cache reuse is the measured proxy for context-injection efficiency (reusing context instead of resending it). Cost per outcome requires connected outcomes, which remain a separate evidence class.

tokenEfficiencyArchitecture: Cache-first context reuse (measured cache share on this profile)
Skill and instruction layering over full-prompt rewrites

contextInjectionSystems: Grok and Claude skills (SKILL.md) for repeatable workflows

problemFocus: Evidence that someone actually operates AI agents deeply

leveragePatterns: Multi-tool orchestration across Claude Code and Codex on the same problems

Work artifacts linked to collector-observed local projects
Evidence classes kept separate: activity, work, identity, outcomes

practice.note: Token-efficiency architecture, context-injection systems, problem focus, and leverage patterns are declared by the member. They are not observed by the collector. Measured efficiency (cache reuse, output share) is a separate evidence class above.

verification.label: Device-signed
verification.basis: The published snapshot was signed by a key held on this device and has not changed since. This proves integrity, not identity, and not that the source logs were genuine.

verification.label: Collector-observed
verification.basis: AI activity was read from the provider's own usage accounting in local logs on this device (156 active days; 8 project(s) seen locally). This is device-local observation, not independent confirmation.

verification.label: Identity-linked
verification.basis: The member published a key-signed proof under an external account; your browser verifies it live (see the identity badge above). This proves control of that account, not legal identity.

verification.label: Provider-attested
verification.basis: No provider has independently confirmed this usage (no OAuth usage API, billing export, or enterprise attestation is connected yet). This is a stronger tier when available.

verification.label: Benchmark-assessed
verification.basis: No practical, reproducible assessment has been completed and attached to this profile.

verification.label: Third-party-confirmed
verification.basis: No client, employer, repository owner, or research organization has confirmed an outcome. 7 artifact(s) are collector-observed, which shows local activity but not authorship, quality, or results.

verification.label: Self-submitted
verification.basis: Identity, headline, links, work artifacts, and any outcomes were entered by the member and are not independently verified.

profile.note: Identity fields are self-submitted and unverified. Activity is derived from measured, provider-reported usage. Activity volume is evidence of practice, not a measure of skill, seniority, or employability.

integrity.note: All automated integrity checks passed. These detect statistical tells, not fraud, and a passing result does not prove the source logs were genuine.

claimAuthority.note: Token volume is evidence of activity, not expertise, productivity, efficiency, or professional value. A valid device signature proves integrity of published bytes and key possession — not source honesty or legal identity.

telemetry.note: Agent-operation telemetry derived from local provider usage events. Counts and timing only — no prompts, responses, tool arguments, paths, or raw session ids. Session identity is an on-device HMAC pseudonym and is not published.
limitations: Provider usage logs do not currently expose full tool-call trees (caller → agent → tools) with payloads.
Timing is inter-event gaps from usage timestamps, not end-to-end wall-clock traces of tool latency.
Session pseudonyms are device-local HMACs; they never leave this machine and are not in the public snapshot.
Codex event-level totals may overstate relative to ccusage aggregates; see EVENT_LEDGER docs.
